Shieldback

A shield-bug's back: a green ground, a scalloped collar across the withers, and a fanning column of ringed eyespots down the topline.

About this gene

Imported from the magic-gene intake, 2026-09-08. The source file is not valid JSON - it has arithmetic in it (`27.0 + "$collarBorderWidth"`), which the format has no notion of. Every computed bound here is written out as a constant or a knob instead.

The collar is a sine band read ACROSS the neck (axis Z) rather than along it, so it scallops round the withers instead of running up the crest. That is the opposite of what the 90/77.94 saw-wave trick does, and it is the right answer for a collar.

Crossing two of them

Finding one

About 1 in 1,724 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Shieldback

The collar is a sine band read ACROSS the neck rather than along it - axis Z, which runs side to side - so it scallops round the withers instead of running up the crest. The eyespots are a ring and a spot on one lattice, cut to the top of the barrel, so they queue down the spine rather than covering the flank.

  1. the ground, a shield-bug green — PARTS, painted with TOWARD
  2. a scalloped collar across the withers — WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  3. a column of ringed eyespots down the topline — RINGS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  4. each with a dark centre — SPOTS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD

Shieldback, coloured

The same back with the ground in a colour the line carries. The eyespots stay red and black - they are the warning, and a warning that matches the animal is not one. Fully recessive.

The eyespots stay red and black in both forms. A warning that matches the animal is not a warning, and letting the hue knob reach them made the gene read as a plain spotted horse.

  1. the ground, a shield-bug green — PARTS, painted with TOWARD
